title: SPCX, TSM, APLD, AMZN, TSLA: Why Retail Traders Couldn’t Take Their Eyes Off These Stocks Last Week - Stocktwits
content: Corporate deals, earnings reports and analyst updates drove stock market activity last week. Investor interest was drawn to SpaceX’s (SPCX) spectrum deal, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.’s (TSM) upcoming earnings, and Applied Digital’s (APLD) better-than-expected revenue. Amazon (AMZN) gained amid reports of job cuts and a possible $7 billion AI startup deal, while Tesla (TSLA) rose on stronger China sales. SpaceX said last week it plans to acquire wireless spectrum from Grain Management that could improve Starlink Mobile’s phone coverage, especially indoors and in areas with weak cellular signals. CEO Elon Musk called the purchase “the last critical piece of the spectrum puzzle”. The deal covers up to 14 MHz of spectrum in the 800 MHz band. The new low-frequency signals can pass through walls and provide phone coverage inside buildings. They will work with Starlink’s existing spectrum, which can handle more data. After getting regulatory approval, SpaceX plans to combine its satellite network with ground-based systems to offer mobile service. JPMorgan said the new spectrum could improve indoor coverage and kept its ‘Overweight’ rating on SpaceX (SPCX). The firm said SpaceX may need to build its own network using cell towers to match the service offered by traditional wireless carriers, unless it partners with a mobile virtual network operator. JPMorgan believes the deal makes Starlink Mobile’s long-term growth potential more realistic and suggests SpaceX’s plans go beyond connecting phones. SpaceX stock gained 2.2% over the week. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment shifted from ‘bullish’ to ‘neutral’ over the past 24 hours. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. reported September 2026 revenue of about NT$511.86 billion ($16.04 billion), down 0.6% from August but up 54.6% year-on-year. TSMC stock fell 4% over the week. Citi analyst Laura Chen raised TSMC’s price target to NT$4,000 from NT$3,800 and maintained a ‘Buy’ rating, flagging the stock as a potential positive catalyst over the next 90 days. The firm expects TSMC to beat its guidance when it reports third-quarter (Q3) results on Oct. 15. Retail sentiment around the stock slipped to ‘bullish’ from ‘extremely bullish’ territory. Last week, Tesla CEO Elon Musk confirmed that Tesla and SpaceX have discussed their Terafab AI chip project with TSMC. He said TSMC could potentially help, but no agreement has been announced and later clarified that TSMC might lease part of the facility but would not take control of the project. Applied Digital reported fiscal Q1 2027 revenue of $341.9 million, a 322% jump from last year, as its AI data center business generated more income. Revenue beat analysts’ expectations of $124.57 million, according to Fiscal.ai data. The company reported an adjusted loss of $0.01 per share, versus an expected loss of $0.28 per share. The company’s high-performance computing hosting business generated $262.6 million, including income from preparing facilities for tenants and rental payments. Its data center hosting business, which serves crypto mining customers, brought in another $37.8 million. However, Applied Digital stock fell 6.7% this week, with retail sentiment remaining ‘extremely bullish’. Amazon stock climbed 4.3% over the week and has eliminated fewer than 1,000 jobs across operations in the U.S., India and the U.K. The reported reductions affect several business areas, including retail, customer service and engineering. According to a Reuters report, Amazon is also changing leadership in its Alexa division after launching new tablets featuring the voice assistant, as the tech giant has struggled to make Alexa profitable since its 2014 launch. Additionally, Amazon is reportedly in talks to buy AI startup Decart in a deal valued at around $7 billion. Tesla sold 95,366 China-manufactured vehicles in September, extending its year-on-year sales growth streak to 11 months despite a decline in global third-quarter deliveries. Separately, the automaker has started replacing its “Full Self-Driving (Supervised)” label with “Tesla Assisted Driving” on European websites following criticism from German officials over the original name's potential to mislead drivers. Tigress Financial maintained a Buy rating and $550 price target on Tesla. The firm expects growth from its self-driving software, Cybercab robotaxis, Optimus robots, energy business and potential SpaceX opportunities. Tesla stock gained 3.2% over the week, but retail sentiment fell to ‘bearish’ from ‘neutral’. So far this year, SPCX, TSM and AMZN stocks gained between 1% and 49%, while APLD and TSLA stocks are down 3% and 14%, respectively. IREN Ltd.’s (IREN) shares jumped 8% in overnight trading late Sunday after a report said that Anthropic is the mystery AI cloud customer the company alluded to during its earnings call a few months ago. The Information published an analysis of the economics of Anthropic’s data center leases, detailing how the AI lab is pushing its cloud partners to accelerate the construction of new data centers. “People familiar with the relationship say Anthropic also has an unannounced multiyear cloud deal with IREN,” The Information said in its report, according to AI Weekly. Anthropic’s push to rapidly expand its computing capacity “increasingly depends on current and former bitcoin miners such as Hut 8, TeraWulf, IREN and Nscale,” the report said. Neither Anthropic nor IREN has commented on the reported partnership. In August, IREN disclosed that it had signed a deal with a leading AI lab but did not identify the customer. “So firstly, customers, new multiyear cloud contracts, including Cohere, Prometheus, Perplexity, Figure AI, Fal AI, Higgsfield AI, and separately, a leading frontier AI lab whose name we’re not able to disclose just yet,” CEO Daniel Roberts said during the company’s fiscal fourth-quarter earnings call. Adding Anthropic to its customer roster would significantly boost IREN, potentially strengthening its position as a provider of AI cloud infrastructure as demand for computing capacity surges. IREN stock came under pressure in the past week after SemiAnalysis raised concerns about the operational quality of the Bitcoin miner-turned-AI infrastructure provider’s legacy data centers in British Columbia. In a series of posts on X on Wednesday, SemiAnalysis said it had heard reports from multiple customers and end users about IREN’s sites in Prince George and Mackenzie, describing them as the “#1 worst site in the industry” according to users. IREN was the top trending ticker on Stocktwits at the time of writing, with a ‘bullish’ retail sentiment and several traders expecting the stock to push higher on Monday. “$IREN one of the companies needs to confirm deal or this is just a pump,” a trader wrote. Another said: “$IREN potential 20% up day coming up for IREN based on the incredible Anthropic news. Been going long since $36.75 in overnight trading. Current trailing stop at $35.95.” IREN is the weakest performer in the neocloud group, which includes CoreWeave (CRWV) and Nebius (NBIS), with shares down nearly 7% year to date. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Comments posted here will also appear on symbol pages. Shares of Sellas Life Sciences (SLS) jumped over 3% overnight late Sunday as retail investors speculated that its 600-square-foot booth at the American Society of Hematology’s (ASH) annual meeting could attract a Big Pharma buyer. SLS shares rose more than 3% Friday to close at $11.65, but still fell 1% for the week, marking their steepest weekly decline in a month. The 68th ASH Annual Meeting and Exposition is scheduled for Dec. 12-Dec. 15 in New Orleans. The meeting brings together blood-disease specialists, researchers and drugmakers to discuss new research and treatments. Sellas is listed at Booth 138, and the exhibit hall is expected to feature more than 275 exhibitors. The ASH floor plan shows major drugmakers across the exhibition halls, including Eli Lilly, Pfizer, Merck, Sanofi, AstraZeneca, GSK, Novartis, AbbVie, Bristol Myers Squibb, Takeda, Genentech, Amgen, Novo Nordisk, Daiichi Sankyo, Astellas, Gilead and Kite Oncology. Sellas’ 20-by-30-foot space sits at the far end of Hall G, directly beside the poster area. Major drugmakers, including Eli Lilly, Takeda, Genentech and AstraZeneca, also occupy large booths in Hall G, while Pfizer, Merck, Sanofi, AbbVie and Bristol Myers Squibb are spread across other halls. Johnson & Johnson is in Hall J, well away from Sellas’ booth. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for SLS has been ‘neutral’ for a week, amid a 20% rise in 24-hour message volume. One user called the booth an “M&A negotiation lounge with an open bar,” then imagined a buyer being told to “sign the papers or another giant will.” Another user, drawing on experience at software conferences, said, “Never did I lease an oversized booth except to announce new product.” A separate user thanked “JNJ for the gigantic booth,” while another speculated that Johnson & Johnson could be a potential suitor. Meanwhile, one user said the booth was “for the partnership… not a BO [buyout].” Another said that the spending could mean Sellas is “desperate for BP [Big Pharma] to take notice.” Sellas is advancing two clinical cancer programs. Its lead candidate, galinpepimut-S (GPS), is an immunotherapy that targets WT1, a protein found in several cancers. The Phase 3 Regal trial is testing GPS in people with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) who entered a second remission after salvage treatment. Regal’s final analysis will begin once 80 participants have died, the trial’s preset threshold. Sellas last reported 78 deaths as of May 11, leaving the study two events short. A separate Phase 2 study is testing SLS009 in newly diagnosed AML, including patients whose disease becomes resistant early to Azacitidine and Venetoclax, a commonly used drug combination. As of Aug. 28, 80 patients had enrolled. Sellas expects initial results in the fourth quarter. Sellas is also exploring SLS009 as a potential treatment for pancreatic cancer. In a patient-derived, lab-grown tumor model resistant to Daraxonrasib, SLS009 produced 17.9% apoptosis, or cancer-cell death, compared with 2.8% with Daraxonrasib alone. Combining the drugs raised apoptosis to 36.5% and necrosis to 30.6%. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Gold advocate Peter Schiff admitted he’s surprised Bitcoin (BTC) has held onto gains that gold has given back, but still expects the cryptocurrency to fall to new lows. Schiff made the comments in an interview with Scott Melker on his podcast, The Wolf Of All Streets, published on Sunday. Both assets surged after the Treasury announced that it would double its long-dated bond buybacks to at least $4 billion per operation. Bitcoin was trading at about $60,000 before that statement and is now close to $85,000, Schiff added. But on the news, gold shot up to around $4,700, then has since cooled off to around $4,000, he added. “I do expect it to make new lows. I just would have thought it would have happened already,” he said. He said that Bitcoin is riding the same technology rally that has boosted the most large-cap stocks. Schiff said that he expects it to fall when the rally fades. Bitcoin’s price was trading around $83,790, up 1% in the last 24 hours. TSMC just had a strong third quarter, with revenue rising 41.2% from a year earlier to $46.7 billion. Net income grew even faster, jumping 68.7%. AI-related chips are driving much of this growth, with high-performance computing accounting for 68% of revenue. The company expects revenue to reach $52.3 billion to $54.3 billion in the fourth quarter and is now forecasting full-year revenue growth of around 44%. What's interesting is that demand isn't coming only from AI accelerators. TSMC is also seeing more demand for CPUs used in AI servers and networking chips. As companies move from chatbots toward AI assistants that can carry out tasks, they may need more computing power. TSMC's CEO said demand for leading-edge chips remains well above what the company can currently supply. The challenge is no longer just keeping up with demand for today's chips, but deciding how much capacity to build for the next few years. Manufacturing advanced chips at scale, with good yields and competitive costs, is extremely difficult. In the third quarter, technologies at 7 nanometers and below accounted for 79% of wafer revenue. Its 2nm process already contributed 8%, and management expects annual capacity for the N2 family to more than double in 2027. Advanced packaging is becoming just as important. As AI chips grow more complex, customers need ways to connect and package multiple components efficiently. TSMC is already producing large packages at good yields and working on even larger designs. It has also committed another $100 billion to US expansion, bringing its planned US investment to $265 billion, and is evaluating further capacity in Texas. These projects bring production closer to customers, but they are expensive. The cost is already showing up in margins. Gross margin fell from 67.7% in the second quarter to 66.4% in the third, mainly because of the 2nm ramp. Overseas factories will add further pressure, with management expecting them to reduce gross margin by 3 to 4 percentage points in the latter part of the coming five-year period. TSMC believes revenue growth will outpace capital spending, but that still needs to play out. The company has also warned that price-sensitive consumer markets are under pressure, so not every part of its business is enjoying the AI boom. TSMC is trading at 33.67x its trailing earnings and 21.41x its future earnings. The difference indicates that analysts expect the company's profits to increase considerably in the coming year. That by itself does not mean the stock is cheap. However, considering the near-monopolistic characteristic of the company, those multiples seem reasonable. There is a good reason for those expectations. Third-quarter net income grew nearly 69% year over year. At 21.41x forward earnings, TSMC doesn't look unreasonable for a business growing this quickly, especially with a 51.1% net margin in the latest quarter. Its manufacturing lead gives it a way to benefit from AI spending. But investors have to look beyond the next few quarters. TSMC's stock weakened even after its latest record results, as the wider chip selloff raised questions about the returns on massive AI infrastructure spending. If customers slow their investment before the new factories reach full production, TSMC could face lower capacity utilization just as its costs rise. That would put pressure on both earnings estimates and the valuation, which would be a double whammy for the stock. The stock's appeal depends on more than strong demand today. The main point is whether earnings can continue to grow fast enough to make the massive investment in new capacity worthwhile. So far, the figures back up the argument.
